AIR: amortised importance sampling over an explicit transform latent¶

Description¶

Question. Can the A↔B transfer be solved with an explicit transform latent, where every learned part targets an exact Bayesian factor and the parts are combined by importance sampling? Earlier learned registration in this repo (notebook 09) did not register. The proposal replaces "learn to move particles" with three parts:

  • a transported decoder $D_\psi$: the predictive and the chain-rule evidence given θ, trained with the true θ;
  • an NPE proposal $q_\phi(\theta\mid A,B)$: a conditional flow, trained with the true θ (forward KL, mass-covering);
  • self-normalized IS, with weights $p(\theta)\hat p(A\mid B,\theta)/q(\theta)$.

The estimator is consistent for any proposal with adequate support. The proposal only changes efficiency (spec §0, §2).

Setup (spec §1–§3, d = 1, phase H0 / Z0; deviations listed below).

  • Prior:
    • $g$ is a random 2-layer tanh MLP (width 32), min–max normalised on 256 points;
    • $T_\theta$ is the time-1 flow of $v_\theta(x) = x(1-x)\sum_j \theta_j\cos((j-1)\pi x)$, with $\theta_j = s_T/j\cdot\tilde\theta_j$, $\tilde\theta\sim N(0, I_J)$, $s_T$ calibrated so that $E|T(x)-x|\approx 0.13$, and RK4;
    • $h = \mathrm{id}$;
    • $N_B = 128$, $n_A\in\{1,\dots,10\}$, 32 queries;
    • noise after $h$ (C2′), with $\sigma_A, \sigma_B \sim U[0.005, 0.03]$.
  • Decoder: 6 layers, $d_{\text{model}} = 128$, 4 heads, a 400-bin bar distribution on $[-0.25, 1.25]$.
    • Masks: B ↔ B; A causal in a random order; x* sees everything; the evidence query $a$ sees B and $A_{<a}$.
    • The null head is the same weights with B masked out.
    • Loss: soft-target CE, trained on a mixture of $J \in \{2,4,8,16\}$ with the true θ.
  • Proposal (one per J): encoder E0, a 4-seed pooled context $c\in\mathbb R^{256}$, and a zuko NSF (5 transforms, hidden 128) over the standardized $\tilde\theta$, trained by NPE. Defensive mixture $\epsilon = 0.1$.
  • Estimator: K draws; evidence averaged over 2 orders of A.
  • References:
    • G-ref: dense-B grid Bayes, $101^2$ over $\tilde\theta\in[-4,4]^2$, $J = 2$;
    • IS-ref: prior IS with the decoder, $K = 4096$, $J = 2$;
    • IS-exact: dense-B IS with $q_{\text{mix}}$, $K = 10^4$, $J > 2$;
    • teacher: the decoder at the true θ (under H0 this is also the spec's "oracle", since $h = \mathrm{id}$);
    • A-only: the null head.
  • Evaluation: 128 fixed tasks per (J, $n_A$), nested in $n_A \in \{1,2,3,5,8,10\}$, 32 queries each.

Deviations from the spec (made before the first run).

  • 128 tasks per $n_A$ instead of 256, and IS-ref with $K = 4096$ instead of 8192 (the overnight budget).
  • Encoder E1 is not run: it needs the "run-2 transport-token module", which is not in this repo. So the E1-vs-E0 question of V5 stays open.
  • RK4 uses 24 steps instead of 16, so that the $J = 16$ inverse error stays below $10^{-4}$ in float32.
  • One decoder serves all J; it is trained on the J-mixture, and it sees θ only through $B_{\text{in}A}$.
  • V6–V8 (d = 2, $h$, relatedness) are out of scope tonight.

What to look for.

  1. V0: the transform family's properties, and G-ref between A-only and the teacher.
  2. V1: teacher vs A-only; evidence fidelity on the $41^2$ grid; permutation spread.
  3. V2: IS-ref vs G-ref.
  4. V3: SBC ranks, HPD coverage, KL(grid ‖ q).
  5. V4: q-IS with $K \in \{8, 32, 128\}$; ESS/K; the error decomposition total = (IS-ref − G-ref) + (q-IS − IS-ref).
  6. V5: ESS/K of q-IS vs prior IS at $K = 32$ across $J \in \{2,4,8,16\}$, and the NLL gap to IS-exact.

Pass criteria (from the spec, §8; nats per query).

  • V0: T is monotone with fixed endpoints; inverse error $< 10^{-4}$; mean $|T(x)-x| \approx 0.13$; G-ref NLL lies between A-only and the teacher/oracle.
  • V1.1: the teacher improves monotonically with $n_A$, and at $n_A = 10$ is within 0.1 of the oracle (trivial under H0).
  • V1.2: median evidence KL < 0.1 nats at every $n_A$; report the 95th percentile of over-rating far from the posterior.
  • V1.3: median permutation spread < 0.05 nats.
  • V2: IS-ref − G-ref ≤ 0.12 nats at every $n_A$.
  • V3: SBC KS $p > 0.01$ per coordinate; 50% / 90% HPD coverage within ±5 points; median KL(grid ‖ q) < 0.2 nats.
  • V4:
    • $\text{NLL}_{q\text{-IS},32} - \text{NLL}_{\text{IS-ref}} \le 0.03$;
    • ESS/K ≥ 0.3;
    • the total gap to G-ref ≤ 0.15 at every $n_A$.
  • V5:
    • ESS/K of q-IS ≥ 0.2 at $J = 16$ while prior IS collapses (expected < 0.01);
    • the NLL gap to IS-exact grows by ≤ 0.05 from $J = 2$ to $J = 16$.

Stop rule (spec §10): if a stage fails, report it with the diagnostics and apply the listed fallback once. Tonight the stages run in one evaluation pass, so failures are reported per stage, and fallbacks are proposed rather than run.

Limits.

  • One seed.
  • G-ref knows $g$ exactly, while the models see 128 noisy B points: that is worth about 0.1 nats at large $n_A$, so G-ref is a floor, not a target.
  • d = 1, H0 and Z0 only.

Report (read this first)¶

Result. Transfer works and the estimator behaves as the theory says, but the pilot fails the pre-registered criteria as written: V1.2, V1.3, V2 (narrowly), V3 (KL, and coverage narrowly), V4 and V5 fail; V0 and V1.1 pass. The largest failures are not a flaw in the idea. They come from an underfit proposal, a budget of K = 32 that is too small for sharp predictives, and a decoder term of about 0.1–0.15 nats.

What held.

  • Transfer. At J = 2, n_A = 1, NLL improves from −0.38 (A-only) to −1.04 (K = 32) and −1.30 (K = 128). q-IS beats prior IS at the same K at every J and n_A.
  • Registration. Mean |T̂ − T| at J = 2 falls from about 0.13 (prior shift) to 0.013 at n_A = 10 (median over tasks).
  • Calibration. SBC passes at J = 2 (it is not a tested criterion at higher J, but no coordinate has p < 0.01), and HPD coverage nearly passes: 56.2 % at J = 2, n_A = 1 is a narrow miss. At J = 4 and 8 the 50 % region over-covers (up to 62 %), which fits a q that is too wide.
  • Consistency. Post hoc, the q-IS loss converges as K grows, to about 0.08–0.13 above G-ref at J = 2, and the gap to IS-exact does not grow with J at K = 2048 (reliable only where IS-exact has ESS > 500).

Why it failed, in order of size (J = 2).

  1. Proposal underfit (fixable, confirmed). q was calibrated but too wide: 1.7–2× the exact posterior's width at n_A ≥ 2 (20k steps). A lossy summary gives exactly this, because calibration does not imply sharpness. Tripling training to 60k improved validation NLL by 0.53 nats (J = 2) and 0.74 (J = 16), raised ESS at every n_A, and cut the median KL(decoder posterior ‖ q) by 16–55 %. It was probably still not converged: the KL limit still fails.
  2. K = 32 is too few draws (fixable at a cost, confirmed in part). Predictives given θ are very sharp, so a small mixture has holes. Even exact posterior draws with Gaussian predictives lose 0.66 nats at K = 32, n_A = 1. This makes the 0.03 limit of V4 at K = 32 close to unreachable there; the decoder's smoother predictives reduce the loss to 0.14. Still, q-IS at K = 32 loses 0.28 more than exact draws with the same decoder at n_A = 1 (60k). That remainder is not isolated. A lower effective K (ESS/K 0.75) is the likely reason, but was not tested. At K = 128 with the 60k proposal, the gap to IS-ref is ≤ 0.01 for n_A ≥ 2 and 0.068 at n_A = 1.
  3. Decoder predictive plus finite B (a floor). With exact posterior draws, the decoder sits 0.07–0.09 above G-ref at all n_A. This matches the ≈ 0.1 finite-B term the spec expects.
  4. Decoder evidence (small in NLL, large in KL). It adds 0.01–0.08 nats on top. Its posterior is about 1.3× wider than exact. Noise-free B removes 21–43 % of the median KL(exact ‖ decoder), so finite noise is part of it, but the V1.2 limit still fails at n_A ≥ 2. Order dependence (V1.3) is real but harmless: 8 orders instead of 2 leave ESS unchanged.

The central claim (V5). Prior IS collapses to its 1/K floor, q-IS does not, but its efficiency does degrade with J and n_A. Measured at K = 2048, where the ESS/K of a sharp posterior is not inflated by the small-K floor, ESS/K at J = 16, n_A = 10 is 5.4 % (60k), not the 14 % seen at K = 32. Cost grows with J; bias does not at J = 16 with the 60k proposal (K = 128 growth ≤ 0.04 at trusted n_A). The 20k J = 4 run does show +0.08 at n_A = 10. So "fixed cost at K = 32" is not supported; "consistent, with a needed K of order 100–2000 that well-trained proposals reduce" is.

Corrected beliefs. Before the diagnostics I expected finite K to be the main cause and the KL failures to be coarse-grid or reference artefacts. The first is only partly true. The second is wrong for the grid: on a fine grid KL(‖q) was unchanged and the decoder's KL rose (0.23 to 0.52 at n_A = 10). The reference mismatch is real but partial.

Limits. One seed, 128 tasks, 32 for fine-grid KL; d = 1, H0, Z0 only; E1, V6–V8 not run. Everything under "Post hoc" was chosen after seeing the results, so it explains the failures but does not re-grade them; the 60k re-evaluation in particular is not a pass of the pre-registered pilot.

def wide(n, J):
    return n[n.J == J].pivot_table(index=["n_a", "task"], columns="method", values="nll")


def gap(w, a, b):
    d = (w[a] - w[b]).groupby("n_a")
    return pd.DataFrame({"mean": d.mean(), "se": d.std() / np.sqrt(d.count())})


def med(d, m, J=2):
    return d[(d.metric == m) & (d.J == J)].groupby("n_a").value.median()


def mean(d, m, J=2):
    return d[(d.metric == m) & (d.J == J)].groupby("n_a").value.mean()


def sbc_p(d):
    r, rng = [], np.random.default_rng(0)
    for (J, m, n), g in d[d.metric.str.startswith("sbc")].groupby(["J", "metric", "n_a"]):
        r.append((J, m, n, kstest((g.value + rng.uniform(size=len(g))) / 256, "uniform").pvalue))
    return pd.DataFrame(r, columns=["J", "coord", "n_a", "p"])


def coverage(d, lv):
    x = d[d.metric == "hpd"]
    return x.assign(c=x.value < lv).groupby(["J", "n_a"]).c.mean().unstack()


print({k: v for k, v in SN.items()})
print("tasks per (J, n_A, method):", nll.groupby(["J", "n_a", "method"]).size().unique())
print("All sweeps ended DONE: 1 decoder, 4 + 2 proposals, 2 eval, 2 diagnose; 0 failed / started / missing.")

Pre-registered criteria, V0–V5¶

In [3]:
def rows(n, d, label):
    w = wide(n, 2)
    t = []
    def add(stage, crit, val, ok):
        t.append({"proposal": label, "stage": stage, "criterion": crit, "measured": val, "pass": bool(ok)})
    gr = w.groupby("n_a").mean()
    add("V0", "G-ref between A-only and teacher", f"n_A=1: {gr.a_only[1]:.2f} > {gr.grid[1]:.2f} > {gr.teacher[1]:.2f}",
        ((gr.grid < gr.a_only) & (gr.grid > gr.teacher)).all())
    tm = gr.teacher
    add("V1.1", "teacher improves with n_A", f"{tm[1]:.3f} -> {tm[10]:.3f}", tm.diff().dropna().le(0).all())
    e = med(diag, "evid_kl")
    add("V1.2", "median evidence KL < 0.1 at every n_A", ", ".join(f"{x:.2f}" for x in e.dropna()), e.dropna().lt(.1).all())
    s = med(diag, "perm_std")
    add("V1.3", "median permutation spread < 0.05", ", ".join(f"{x:.3f}" for x in s.dropna()), s.dropna().lt(.05).all())
    g = gap(w, "isref", "grid")["mean"]
    add("V2", "IS-ref - G-ref <= 0.12 at every n_A", ", ".join(f"{x:.3f}" for x in g), g.le(.12).all())
    p = sbc_p(d); pp = p[p.J == 2].p.min()
    add("V3", "SBC KS p > 0.01 (J=2)", f"min p = {pp:.3f}", pp > .01)
    c5, c9 = coverage(d, .5).loc[2], coverage(d, .9).loc[2]
    add("V3", "HPD 50/90 within +-5 points", f"50: {c5.min():.3f}-{c5.max():.3f}; 90: {c9.min():.3f}-{c9.max():.3f}",
        ((c5 - .5).abs().le(.05).all() and (c9 - .9).abs().le(.05).all()))
    k = med(d, "kl_grid_q")
    add("V3", "median KL(grid||q) < 0.2", ", ".join(f"{x:.2f}" for x in k), k.lt(.2).all())
    a = gap(w, "qis32", "isref")["mean"]
    add("V4", "q-IS32 - IS-ref <= 0.03", ", ".join(f"{x:.3f}" for x in a), a.le(.03).all())
    ess = mean(d, "ess_qis32")
    add("V4", "ESS/K >= 0.3 (K=32)", f"min over n_A {ess.min():.2f}", ess.min() >= .3)
    tg = gap(w, "qis32", "grid")["mean"]
    add("V4", "total gap to G-ref <= 0.15", ", ".join(f"{x:.3f}" for x in tg), tg.le(.15).all())
    e16 = mean(d, "ess_qis32", 16)
    add("V5", "ESS/K of q-IS >= 0.2 at J=16 (K=32)", ", ".join(f"{x:.2f}" for x in e16), e16.ge(.2).all())
    w16 = wide(n, 16)
    gx = gap(w16, "qis32", "isexact")["mean"] - gap(w, "qis32", "grid")["mean"]
    trusted = med(d, "ess_isexact", 16).ge(500)
    add("V5", "gap growth J=2 -> 16 <= 0.05 (trusted n_A: IS-exact ESS > 500)",
        ", ".join(f"n={i}: {x:+.2f}" for i, x in gx[trusted].items()), gx[trusted].le(.05).all())
    return pd.DataFrame(t)

Prior IS ESS/K at K=32, J=16 (floor 1/32 = 0.031; the spec's '< 0.01' cannot occur at this K): {1: 0.213, 2: 0.11, 3: 0.074, 5: 0.055, 8: 0.046, 10: 0.039}
IS-exact median ESS, J=16 (20k): {1: 3712.0, 2: 1521.0, 3: 638.0, 5: 260.0, 8: 66.0, 10: 43.0}
V1.2 over-rating p95 (J=2): {1: 1158.0, 2: 2713.0, 5: 6481.0, 10: 11738.0}
Median t_err J=2: {1: 0.0854, 2: 0.0603, 3: 0.0466, 5: 0.0268, 8: 0.0159, 10: 0.0127}

Reading the table. The pass column applies the criteria literally. Standard errors are about 0.03 for V2 and 0.05–0.07 for the small-n_A V4 values, so V2's 0.159 / 0.144 is a narrow failure. Three criteria need care:

  • V1.2's over-rating runs to thousands of nats. Read this as a property of the exact Gaussian likelihood's far tail (σ_A can be 0.005), compared with a bar distribution whose log density is bounded, not as a sign of over-rated transforms. KL is the informative number.
  • V5's prior criterion ("< 0.01") cannot be met at K = 32 because ESS/K ≥ 1/K. Prior IS sits at that floor, so it has collapsed.
  • V5's gap is only testable at n_A where IS-exact has ESS > 500. With fewer effective draws IS-exact itself moves: at J = 16, n_A = 10, it was −1.885 with the 20k proposal and −1.993 with the 60k proposal.

Example tasks: prior samples of A and B, and the predictive¶

Two evaluation tasks (J = 2; they are prior draws), with the pre-registered checkpoints (decoder pilot_20261102-151834, proposal -151837, member 0).

  • Top left: task B. The true g, B's 128 noisy points, and A's true function f_A = g ∘ T for comparison.
  • Bottom left: the transform. The true T, and 30 transforms drawn from q at n_A = 10 (the registration).
  • Other panels: the predictive density over a grid of x_A,test (200 points × 400 bins). Each column is normalised to its maximum, so the shape is visible where the predictive is sharp. Overlays: the true f_A, A's points and the predictive mean. Top row: AIR, q-IS with K = 128. Bottom row: the A-only null head (same network, B removed). n_A grows left to right (nested designs).

This cell needs the checkpoints in runs/air/ (not in git); it runs on CPU in about a minute.

In [5]:
import dataclasses

import torch
from matplotlib.colors import LinearSegmentedColormap

from meta_pfn.experimental.air.decoder import N_BINS, Y_HI, Y_LO, Decoder
from meta_pfn.experimental.air.estimator import importance
from meta_pfn.experimental.air.prior import flow
from meta_pfn.experimental.air.proposal import Proposal
from meta_pfn.experimental.air.train import eval_tasks

CK = ROOT / "runs/air"
DEC_CK = CK / "pilot_20261102-151834/0/tracking/artifacts/model.pt"
Q_CK = CK / "pilot_20261102-151837/0/tracking/artifacts/model.pt"
if not (DEC_CK.exists() and Q_CK.exists()):
    print("Checkpoints not found under runs/air/; rsync them from the run host to draw the example tasks.")
else:
    torch.manual_seed(0)
    dec = Decoder(D=128, layers=6)
    dec.load_state_dict(torch.load(DEC_CK, map_location="cpu"))
    q = Proposal(2)
    q.load_state_dict(torch.load(Q_CK, map_location="cpu"))
    dec.eval(), q.eval()
    XS = torch.linspace(0, 1, 200)
    CEN = (torch.linspace(Y_LO, Y_HI, N_BINS + 1)[:-1] + (Y_HI - Y_LO) / N_BINS / 2).numpy()
    CMAP = LinearSegmentedColormap.from_list("seq", ["#fcfcfb", "#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#2a78d6", "#184f95", "#0d366b"])

    @torch.no_grad()
    def ppd(t, K=128):
        tg = dataclasses.replace(t, xq=XS[None], yq=torch.zeros(1, len(XS)), fq=torch.zeros(1, len(XS)))
        th, lqm = q.sample_mix(t.xb, t.yb, t.xa, t.ya, K)
        w = importance(dec, tg, th, lqm)["lw"][0].softmax(-1)
        xb_t = flow(t.xb.expand(K, -1), th[0], t.s_t, inverse=True)
        rep = lambda z: z.expand(K, -1)  # noqa: E731
        lg, _ = dec(xb_t, rep(t.yb), rep(t.xa), rep(t.ya), rep(XS[None]))
        p1 = (w[:, None, None] * lg.softmax(-1)).sum(0)
        lg0, _ = dec(xb_t[:1], t.yb, t.xa, t.ya, XS[None], use_b=False)
        return p1.numpy(), lg0.softmax(-1)[0].numpy(), th[0]

    def heat(ax, p, t, title):
        img = p / p.max(1, keepdims=True)
        ax.imshow(img.T, origin="lower", aspect="auto", extent=[0, 1, Y_LO, Y_HI], cmap=CMAP, vmin=0, vmax=1, interpolation="nearest")
        fa = t.g(flow(XS[None], t.theta, t.s_t))[0]
        ax.plot(XS, fa, color=INK, lw=1.5, label="true f_A")
        ax.plot(XS, p @ CEN, color=C[1], lw=1.5, ls="--", label="PPD mean")
        ax.scatter(t.xa[0], t.ya[0], s=40, color=C[3], edgecolor=INK, lw=.8, zorder=3, label="A points")
        ax.set(xlim=(0, 1), ylim=(-0.1, 1.1))
        ax.set_title(title, loc="left", fontsize=9)
        ax.grid(False)

    base = eval_tasks(2, 128, 777, "cpu")
    for i in (0, 1):
        ti = base.sub(slice(i, i + 1))
        fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 4, figsize=(13, 6.2), sharex=True)
        u = flow(XS[None], ti.theta, ti.s_t)
        a = axs[0, 0]
        a.plot(XS, ti.g(XS[None])[0], color=INK, lw=1.5, label="true g (B)")
        a.scatter(ti.xb[0], ti.yb[0], s=10, color=C[0], label="B points")
        a.plot(XS, ti.g(u)[0], color=C[1], lw=1.5, ls=":", label="true f_A = g∘T")
        a.set(ylim=(-0.1, 1.1), ylabel="y")
        a.set_title(f"task {i}: B (σ_B = noise) and f_A", loc="left", fontsize=9)
        a.legend(fontsize=7, loc="best")
        for col, n in enumerate((1, 3, 10), start=1):
            t = ti.head(n)
            p1, p0, th = ppd(t)
            heat(axs[0, col], p1, t, f"AIR (q-IS, K=128), n_A = {n}")
            heat(axs[1, col], p0, t, f"A-only, n_A = {n}")
            if n == 10:
                b = axs[1, 0]
                for k in range(30):
                    b.plot(XS, flow(XS[None], th[k:k + 1], t.s_t)[0] - XS, color=C[0], lw=.8, alpha=.35)
                b.plot(XS, (u - XS[None])[0], color=INK, lw=1.8, label="true T(x) − x")
                b.plot([], [], color=C[0], lw=.8, label="30 draws of q, n_A = 10")
                b.set(ylabel="T(x) − x", xlabel="x")
                b.set_title("registration: T(x) − x", loc="left", fontsize=9)
                b.legend(fontsize=7)
        axs[0, 1].legend(fontsize=7, loc="upper left")
        for a in axs[1, 1:]:
            a.set_xlabel("x_A,test")
        fig.suptitle(f"Example task {i} (J = 2): predictive density over x_A,test, column-normalised", x=.01, ha="left", fontsize=11)
        fig.tight_layout()
        plt.show()

Registration, step by step: proposed draws ("slots") and their importance weights¶

AIR does not refine hypotheses iteratively, so there are no intermediate registration steps. Registration is a single draw from q followed by reweighting. The closest analogue of the earlier designs' slots is the K = 128 draws of θ:

  1. q proposes them (point positions);
  2. the decoder's chain-rule evidence weights them (point size and colour = normalised weight);
  3. the predictive is the weighted mixture.

Shown for example task 0 as n_A grows: top, θ space, with the exact dense-B posterior (G-ref, grey contours at 50 / 90 / 99 % mass) and the true θ (black cross). Bottom, the same draws as T(x) − x curves. The darker the curve, the higher the weight; the true T is black. ESS/K is in each title.

from matplotlib.colors import Normalize

from meta_pfn.experimental.air import reference as R

if DEC_CK.exists() and Q_CK.exists():
    torch.manual_seed(1)
    ti = base.sub(slice(0, 1))
    g_pts = R.grid(101)
    fig, axs = plt.subplots(2, 3, figsize=(12.5, 7.2))
    for col, n in enumerate((1, 3, 10)):
        t = ti.head(n)
        with torch.no_grad():
            th, lqm = q.sample_mix(t.xb, t.yb, t.xa, t.ya, 128)
            r = importance(dec, t, th, lqm)
        w = r["lw"][0].softmax(-1).numpy()
        ess = 1 / (w**2).sum() / len(w)
        th = th[0]
        post = R.grid_ref(t, 0, g_pts)["logpost"].exp().reshape(101, 101).numpy()
        ps = np.sort(post.ravel())[::-1]
        lv = [ps[np.searchsorted(ps.cumsum(), m)] for m in (0.99, 0.9, 0.5)]
        ax = axs[0, col]
        gx = np.linspace(-4, 4, 101)
        ax.contour(gx, gx, post.T, levels=sorted(set(lv)), colors=MUTED, linewidths=1)
        o = np.argsort(w)
        ax.scatter(th[o, 0], th[o, 1], s=8 + 400 * w[o], c=w[o], cmap=CMAP, norm=Normalize(0, w.max()), edgecolor=INK, lw=.3, zorder=3)
        ax.scatter(*t.theta[0].numpy(), marker="x", s=90, color=INK, lw=2, zorder=4)
        ax.set(xlim=(-4, 4), ylim=(-4, 4), xlabel="θ̃₁", ylabel="θ̃₂" if col == 0 else None, aspect="equal")
        ax.set_title(f"n_A = {n}: q draws sized by weight, ESS/K = {ess:.2f}", loc="left", fontsize=9)
        b = axs[1, col]
        cur = (flow(XS[None].expand(len(w), -1), th, t.s_t) - XS[None]).numpy()
        for k in o:
            b.plot(XS, cur[k], color=CMAP(0.15 + 0.85 * w[k] / w.max()), lw=.6 + 2 * w[k] / w.max(), alpha=.8)
        b.plot(XS, (flow(XS[None], t.theta, t.s_t) - XS[None])[0], color=INK, lw=2, label="true T(x) − x")
        b.scatter(t.xa[0], np.zeros(n) + b.get_ylim()[0], marker="|", s=120, color=C[3], lw=2, label="A's x", zorder=4, clip_on=False)
        b.set(xlabel="x", ylabel="T(x) − x" if col == 0 else None)
        b.set_title("same draws as transforms (dark = high weight)", loc="left", fontsize=9)
    axs[1, 0].legend(fontsize=7, loc="lower left")
    fig.suptitle("Registration in AIR: one proposal step, then importance weights (example task 0, J = 2)", x=.01, ha="left", fontsize=11)
    fig.tight_layout()
    plt.show()

Review questions (2026-11-03)¶

Four questions from reading the example plots, checked with code:

  1. Is A-only the same network? Yes: use_b=False masks B out of the same weights (decoder.py). It was trained jointly as a second forward pass.
  2. Why do the predictives put mass on 0 and 1 at the edges? Is the prior biased there? The cell below measures it.
  3. How many A points pin T down? For these plots T has J = 2 parameters. The cell counts posterior modes as n_A grows.
  4. In example task 0, n_A = 3, why is the wrong mode weighted higher? The cell splits the posterior along its ridge.

Answers.

  1. A-only is the same network and weights, with B masked out. That matches the project's same-model rule (decision 0002).
  2. The edges come from the prior, not the network. Each g is a tanh MLP min–max normalised on [0, 1]. So every function reaches exactly 0 and 1, and in about half the draws the max (or the min) is at an endpoint. At x = 0 and x = 1, about 80 % of the prior mass lies in y < 0.2 or y > 0.8, against about 40 % at x = 0.5. T fixes the endpoints, so f_A inherits this. A Bayes-correct predictive therefore pushes unobserved edges towards 0 or 1. With one point at the right edge (A-only, n_A = 1), the right side is pinned and the left keeps the U-shaped prior marginal. In task 0 at n_A = 10, no A value exceeds about 0.2, yet the max must equal 1. The only large unobserved gap is [0, 0.24], so the predictive rises to 1 there, and correctly. This is a strong and unrealistic feature of the prior (inherited from runs 1–2). It makes edges unusually informative and could flatter any method. Whether to keep it is a prior-design decision for the next pre-registration.
  3. Two parameters, yet not pinned by two points. Width shrinks quickly (about 0.24 of the prior width at n_A = 2, 0.04 at n_A = 10), but because g is not monotone, distinct transforms can fit the same points. Separate posterior modes persist in about a quarter of tasks at n_A = 3 and about a fifth at n_A = 10. At J = 2, roughly J points plus a few to break mode ambiguity is the practical rule. For higher J, the directions the A points do not constrain stay at prior width, which matters only where predictions depend on them.
  4. Weighting the wrong mode is Bayes-correct here. Both ends of the ridge fit the three points. The likelihood alone puts about two thirds of the mass on the true side (it is broader there), but its peak is higher on the other side, and the prior is about 3 times higher there. The true θ̃₂ = 2.84 is a 2.8 σ draw. The exact posterior puts 13 % on the true side, and the decoder's posterior 13 %. So the decoder reproduces the exact weighting, and the "wrong" mode is what an ideal learner would favour from three points.

Post hoc: why the stages failed¶

Not pre-registered; added after seeing the table above, on the user's standing instruction to investigate failures. Sweeps: pilot_20261102-165535 (diagnostics, 20k proposals), -165541 (60k proposals for J = 2, 16), -183335 (their V0–V5 evaluation), -183338 (their diagnostics).

1. Error decomposition¶

Uses the spec's §7 terms, with IS-ref split further by exact-posterior draws through the decoder at K = 128 (a slight upper bound on the decoder term, since K is finite).

fig, axs = plt.subplots(1, 3, figsize=(10.5, 3.7), sharey=True)
gridn = mean(pf, "nll_grid")
for ax, n in zip(axs, [1, 3, 10]):
    def cur(d, pref):
        x = d[(d.J == 2) & (d.n_a == n) & d.metric.str.match(pref + r"\d+$")]
        s = x.groupby("metric").value.mean()
        s.index = [int(i.replace(pref, "")) for i in s.index]
        return s.sort_index() - gridn[n]
    for s, l, c, k in [(cur(pf, "nll_qis"), "q-IS, 20k", C[1], "s"), (cur(pf6, "nll_qis"), "q-IS, 60k", C[2], "^"),
                       (cur(pf, "nll_dec_post"), "exact draws, decoder", C[0], "o"),
                       (cur(pf, "nll_exact_post"), "exact draws, exact predictive", C[3], "D")]:  # fmt: skip
        s = s[s.index >= 32]
        ax.plot(s.index, s.values, color=c, marker=k, label=l)
    ax.set_xscale("log", base=2)
    ax.set_title(f"n_A = {n}", loc="left", fontsize=10)
    ax.set_xlabel("K (draws)")
axs[0].set_ylabel("NLL above G-ref (nats)")
axs[0].legend(fontsize=8)
fig.suptitle("A perfect proposal also needs K > 32, but q-IS still loses more (J=2, post hoc)", x=.01, ha="left", fontsize=11)
fig.tight_layout()
plt.show()

4. Proposal and evidence fidelity on a fine local grid¶

An 81² grid fitted to each task, 32 tasks. This excludes coarse-grid artefacts: the KLs do not fall, so grid resolution was not the problem.

Proposed verdict (not recorded; the user runs decide)¶

Proposed: NO-GO on the pilot as pre-registered (sweep pilot_20261102-162127): V1.2, V1.3, V2, V3, V4 and V5 fail. The failures do not refute the idea. Consistency, calibration, registration and non-growing bias all held, and the largest losses shrink with more proposal training and with K.

Next steps, by expected value.

  1. Train the proposal to a real plateau, then measure the K needed for V4's 0.03 at n_A = 1, where the gap is still open.
  2. Re-state V4/V5 at a K that a perfect proposal can meet (K ≈ 128 rather than 32), as a new pre-registration.
  3. Test whether the n_A = 1 remainder is the effective K, and whether a less sharp predictive (for example marginalising a small θ jitter per draw) closes it. This is an idea, not a result.
  4. Keep the listed V1 fallback (a small training residual) in reserve; decoder evidence costs at most 0.08 nats, so it is not the priority.
